dataset.name: Plant root trait measurements raw data, 1962-2018, Island of Puerto Rico
description: This data package is a compilation of studies and raw datasets on root traits including root biomass, root nitrogen and phosphorus concentrations organized by different root diameters, species, soil depth, and forest types in Puerto Rico. The attached zip file contains a metadata document "archive metadata.docx" in Word document and PDF formats that describe the methods of data collection, the data sources and publications used in the synthesis, and information about the contents of the two CSV data files "root.shoot.ratio_PR.csv" and "Raw data.csv." Also included are a KMZ file with data collection locations and an additional CSV file with coordinates for each site of data collection organized by data author and year of publication.
This dataset was originally published on the NGEE Tropics Archive and is being mirrored on ESS-DIVE for long-term archival
Acknowledgement: USDA Forest Service - International Institute of Tropical Forestry.

citation: Frangi & Lugo (1985), Murphy & Lugo (1986), Cuevas et al. (1991), and Lugo (1992), Colón (2006) and Teh, Silver & Scatena (2009), Gale & Grigal (1987), Cairns et al. (1997), Mokany et al. (2006), (RStudio Team, (2016)
These publications provided raw data and models for this dataset. Further details can be found in the attached word document titled "archive metadata.docx"
measurementTechnique:
Data was collected from search engines Google Scholar, Web of Science, and Scopus. We looked at all papers returned when searching for the key words: "root", "below ground", "plant", and "Puerto Rico". FRED (Fine Root Ecology Database Version 2) and ORNL DAAC (Oak Ridge National Laboratory Distributed Active Archive Center) were used to compare Puerto Rico's data with other tropical/global studies.
Fine roots were defined as all roots less than or equal to 2 mm in diameter. Root:shoot ratio was collected using whole tree sampling. Puerto Rico root:shoot ratio was compared with global metanalyses we used the formula from the methods of Cairns et al. (1997) and Mokany et al. (2006).
All statistical analyses were performed in R studio. We used ANOVA to compare root:shoot ratio as well as N and P among species.
Further methods are detailed in the word document included in the attached zip file.
